title: Russian — ALA-LC (Library of Congress, 2012)
authority: Library of Congress / American Library Association, Russian romanization table (2012 version)
description: Library of Congress / American Library Association romanization used in library catalogues, with diacritics and ligature ties: Ё→Ë, Й→Ĭ, Ц→T͡S, Э→Ė, Ю→I͡U, Я→I͡A, Ъ→ʺ, Ь→ʹ.
notes: Tie = U+0361 (t͡s, i͡u, i͡a). Library catalogues often encode it as the MARC half marks U+FE20/U+FE21.

Following the LoC table and catalogue practice, both letters under a tie are capitalized when the Cyrillic letter is capital (Ц→T͡S, Ю→I͡U, Я→I͡A: I͡Akutsk, T͡Svetaeva); iuliia writes I͡ulii͡a with a lower-case second letter. This is done with a post rule.
Since the 2012 revision Ъ is romanized ʺ everywhere, including word-final (before 2012 it was dropped at word end).
Pre-1918 letters: І→ī, Ѣ→i͡e, Ѳ→ḟ, Ѵ→ẏ.
iuliia's JSON outputs Cyrillic ё for Ё (data bug); this scheme uses Latin ë (U+00EB).
